test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 01 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which two countries signed a treaty in late May 2025, transferring sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago?
solution:
The correct answer is __**UK and Mauritius**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Chagos Archipelago** is a group of seven atolls comprising more than 60 individual tropical islands in the Indian Ocean. It has been a disputed territory between the **United Kingdom and Mauritius**.
 
• In **1965**, the UK separated the Chagos Archipelago from Mauritius before granting Mauritius independence in 1968, creating the **British Indian Ocean Territory (BIOT)**.
 
• The sovereignty of the Chagos Archipelago has been a contentious issue for decades. In 2019, the **International Court of Justice (ICJ)** ruled that the UK’s continued occupation of the islands was **illegal** and that the archipelago should be returned to Mauritius.
 
• On **May 2025**, the UK and Mauritius signed a **treaty** to transfer the sovereignty of the Chagos Archipelago to Mauritius, marking a significant geopolitical development in the region.
 
• This treaty is seen as a step toward resolving a long-standing colonial dispute and fulfilling the ICJ’s advisory opinion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of the Dispute:**

 
 
• The Chagos Archipelago was separated from Mauritius by the UK in **1965**, three years before Mauritius gained independence.
 
• The UK established a military base on Diego Garcia, the largest island in the archipelago, in partnership with the United States. The local population was forcibly removed to make way for the base.
 
 
 
• **International Court of Justice (ICJ) Advisory Opinion:**
 
 
• In **2019**, the ICJ concluded that the UK’s decolonization process of Mauritius was incomplete and that the UK must return the Chagos Archipelago to Mauritius.
 
• The ICJ’s ruling was supported by the **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)**, which passed a resolution in favor of Mauritius.
 
 
 
• **Diego Garcia and Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• Diego Garcia serves as a critical military base for the **United States**, playing a key role in regional security and global operations.
 
• The treaty ensures that the US will retain access to the base under a long-term lease agreement even after the sovereignty transfer.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Implications:**
 
 
• The treaty marks a significant step in addressing **post-colonial grievances**, strengthening Mauritius’s sovereignty.
 
• It may influence similar sovereignty disputes worldwide, setting a precedent for decolonization and territorial negotiations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Support:** Many countries, including **India**, supported Mauritius’s claim over the Chagos Archipelago in the UNGA resolution.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** The treaty ensures commitments to protect the ecological integrity of the archipelago, which is home to rare marine biodiversity.
 
• **Historical Context:** The forced displacement of the Chagossians remains a contentious issue, and the treaty includes provisions for their potential resettlement.
